name: Dhokar Dalna
subtitle: diamonds of fried chana dal cake simmered in a gingery potato gravy

ingredients.qty: 3, 2 ground into the dal paste and 1 slit

ingredients.note: for a gluten-free dish use compounded-free hing

prepNotes: Soak the chana dal 5 hours or overnight, then drain it thoroughly.
Grind the drained dal with 2 green chillies and 1 tbsp of the ginger to a coarse, sandy paste using as little water as possible. A wet paste will never set.
Oil a plate or tray before you start cooking the dal; the mixture has to be spread while it is still hot.
The cake must cool completely, at least 30 minutes, before you cut and fry it.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai, add 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, the nigella and half the asafoetida, and let them crackle for 15 seconds.
Add the dal paste with 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt. Stir constantly over medium heat for 10-12 minutes.
steps.tip: It is done when the paste stops sticking to the pan and rolls into a single ball behind the spoon.

steps.text: Tip the hot mixture onto the oiled tray and press it flat to about 1.5cm with the back of a wet spoon. Cool 30 minutes, then cut into diamonds.
steps.tip: Pressing while hot is what makes the dhoka hold together. Once it cools it will crack instead.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil and fry the diamonds in batches, 2-3 minutes a side, until crusted and deep gold, handling them with a flat spatula. Drain and set aside.
In the same pan fry the potato quarters with a pinch of turmeric for 5 minutes until golden. Set aside.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil, the bay leaves, remaining cumin seeds and asafoetida, and crackle 15 seconds.
Add the remaining ginger paste and cook 1 minute, then the tomato puree and all the ground spices.
Fry this masala 6-8 minutes, sprinkling in a tablespoon of water whenever it sticks, until the oil separates at the edges.
steps.tip: This is the bhuna stage and it cannot be hurried. Undercooked masala tastes raw and dusty.

steps.text: Add the potatoes, 600ml water, the slit chilli, sugar and salt. Simmer covered 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Slide in the fried dhoka pieces and simmer uncovered 3-4 minutes only.
steps.tip: Add them at the very end. Any longer and they drink the gravy and fall apart.

steps.text: Finish with the garam masala and ghee, rest 5 minutes, and serve with rice.

storage: The fried dhoka keeps 3 days refrigerated on its own; the gravy keeps 3 days too. Combine and warm through just before serving rather than storing them together.
